_description: Layout library of the layout analysis, by KeyboardEvent.code. An entry with « keys » is an alphabetic block (3 rows, base characters only), imported on 2026-11-14 from the Oxeylyzer layout set (Apache-2.0 repository) and, for the classics it lacks, from the cmini collection (GPL-3.0 repository), and on 2026-11-17 from genkey's layouts (GPL-3.0 repository) by tools/build/import-genkey-layouts.cjs; the codegen completes it with the US number row and the US Shift pairs (letters: upper case). An entry with « rows » may state « dead_keys » (a character of its rows → a standard accent of layout_formats.js): a KLA file cannot say that a key is dead, so each is stated where the layout types that accent's letters nowhere else (Optimot, BvoFRak and the Spanish QWERTY: ê, á or ü only through ^, ´ or ¨), and the codegen composes it by Unicode normalisation as the Studio's importers do. An entry with « rows » is a whole layout (base, Shift, AltGr, Shift+AltGr of every key its file states), imported on 2026-11-17 from Keyboard Layout Analyzer's built-in layouts (MIT repository) by tools/build/import-kla-layouts.cjs; the codegen takes it as it is. Only the arrangements are re-encoded, never a file, on the basis given in docs/audits/layout-analysers/report.md, section « Layout library ». « source » and « source_path » name the file each layout comes from; « not_imported » lists the files of these collections left out, with the reason and, for a duplicate, the library layout with the same keys (« same_as »). An entry re-encoded from the layout's official files (« source » optimot, xkeyboard_config, neo_layout or engram, imported on 2026-11-18) states its dead keys as cells ({"dead": state}) and their compositions as « dead_rules » (the second key's character, or « dead:<state> » for a dead key, → the output, taken from the layout's XCompose over the libX11 en_US.UTF-8 Compose table, or from its README); a standard accent's state composes by normalisation what its rules leave out, and sequences of three keys or more are left out. The Neo family's four levels are Neo's levels 1, 2, 3 and 5 (Mod3 stands for AltGr), without level 4, which needs Mod4. The registry layouts (static/layouts/registry) and the reference QWERTY and AZERTY (layout_composer/reference_layouts.js) join the library at codegen with all their layers and dead keys, so they are not repeated here.
